configuration: Upstream P2 DG Euler Sod shock (512 cells) through t=0.1 as a fluid species of the vlasov app.
observable: the final conserved-variable and primitive-variable frames of the fluid species
variant: ic/variant/value.txt changes rhol from 3.0 to 3.000000000000001, exactly two upward binary64 ULP.
altbuild: run.sh altbuild runs the nominal inputs on the same pinned source compiled strict-IEEE with the same gcc (-O2, no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native: the build-ieee/ tree of the oracle image); a correct port compiled without fast-math or FMA contraction is exactly such a build, so its distance from the default -O3 -ffast-math -march=native build is the floor a candidate must be allowed.

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck on 2026-09-07: run.sh altbuild (same source, gcc -O2 strict IEEE: no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native (build-ieee/)) against run.sh nominal, graded with the check's own validate.py: all graded values within bound

altbuild.what: same source, gcc -O2 strict IEEE: no -ffast-math, -ffp-contract=off, no -march=native (build-ieee/)

warrant: The graded histories and frames follow the DG fluid-species path of the vlasov app: the modal Euler flux, the primitive-variable recovery and the fluid time stepper (`gkyl_vlasov_fluid_species`), used by 24 drivers and by no other check. In `rt_dg_euler_sodshock_p2.c`, `rhol` (line 63) is the left-state density of the Riemann problem; the two-ULP variant therefore moves every graded value at the level of the arithmetic, while a wrong Euler flux, a wrong primitive-variable recovery or a wrong limiter changes them at order one. The bound atol=1e-07, rtol=1e-07 was set on 2026-09-06 from the calibration selfcheck on the x86 worker 136.114.2.6 (1 cpu, 4 GB, Docker): the two-ULP variant used at most 3.1e-3 of it and the strict-IEEE altbuild at most 1.1e-3 (worst files `euler.gkyl` and `euler.gkyl`), a headroom of about 324x over the larger legitimate perturbation, while the faults named above move the graded values at order one.
